title: flashtrace JSON report
description: A flashtrace run reported as JSON (--format json). Format version 0 is unstable: while flashtrace is pre-1.0 this schema changes in place, breaking changes included. Unknown fields are deliberately left unconstrained, so consumers and validators must tolerate them.

schemaVersion.description: Integer version of this format. 0 means unstable: no compatibility promise until flashtrace 1.0.0, which starts the format at 1.

flashtrace.description: Version of the flashtrace that produced the document. Provenance only.

ok.description: Run verdict: true iff no item is defective and no problem occurred. Matches the exit code (0 iff true).

items.description: Every item regardless of status, sorted by file, line, character.

forwards.description: Every forwarding declaration, voided ones included, sorted by file, line, character.

problems.description: Parse- and analysis-level problems, sorted by file, line, character.

character.description: 1-based column of the first character of the construct.

file.description: Path relative to the working directory, with forward slashes on every platform.

title.description: The heading above a spec item; null if there is none and always null for code items.

tags.description: The item's Tags entries; always [] for code items.

status.description: defective: at least one defect; shallow-covered: no defects, but not deep-covered; deep-covered otherwise.

needs.description: One entry per declared Needs reference, in declaration order.

covers.description: One entry per declared Covers reference, in declaration order.

forwardsTo.description: ID of the effective forwarding target, or null.

wantedBy.description: The items whose declared needs resolve to this item, sorted by file, line, character. Declared needs only: an item wanted solely because a forwarding targets it has an empty wantedBy, so this array is not a test for whether an item is wanted - the unwanted-item defect is.

ref.description: The reference exactly as declared; may carry a wildcard revision.

resolvedTo.description: Full IDs of the defined items matching the reference, in ascending revision order. The need is covered exactly when this is non-empty.

ref.description: The (always concrete) covered ID as declared.

status.description: valid: the target exists and needs this item's ID; orphaned: the target does not exist; unwanted: the target exists but does not need this item's ID.

kind.description: What is wrong, one kind per condition, so kind alone tells every defect apart. uncovered-need: a declared need matches no defined item. uncovered-forward: the forwarding target does not exist. orphaned-cover: a covers entry points at an item that does not exist. unwanted-cover: a covers entry points at an existing item that does not need this one. unwanted-item: no item needs this code item. duplicate-id: this full ID is defined more than once. duplicate-forwarding: more than one forwarding is declared for this item.

ref.description: The ID the defect is about: the needed, covered or forwarded-to ID; for unwanted-item, duplicate-id and duplicate-forwarding, the item's own ID.

message.description: The defect worded exactly as the plain-text report words it. Offered so a consumer can present the same text; kind and ref carry the same information as data, so the message is never worth parsing and may be reworded without kind changing.

existingRevisions.description: Present exactly when the revision-mismatch hint applies: defined revisions of the same type:group/name, bare (without '#'), ascending.

effective.description: True iff the declaration is in effect; the items' forwardsTo fields mirror exactly the effective entries.

problem.description: A parse- or analysis-level problem; any problem makes the run fail.

shallowCoveredItems.description: Ok items that are not deep-covered.

problems.description: Number of entries in the top-level problems array.
